newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore-based consumers seen mulling purchases.
newsitem.headline: Singapore-based consumers seen mulling purchases.

text.p: Trading in the Singapore rubber market was quiet by midsession on Monday, but major consumers are said to be considering making some purchases later this afternoon, dealers said.

"The big boys may decide to pick up something later. They'll be taking a look at this market later on," a dealer said, adding they would likely buy SIR20 rubber after a deal was concluded in Palembang at around 49.00 U.S. cents a lb.
The Songkran Buddhist holidays in Thailand, the world's biggest natural rubber producer, was weighing on the market. "That will make the situation worse," one trader said.
The market will be further depressed when the Eid Al-Adha Moslem holidays shuts down markets in Singapore, Malaysia and Indonesia on Friday, dealers said.
"It's very quiet this morning. We'll only probably see some kind of activity in the last two hours of trading," one said.
At around 0430 GMT, June RSS3 was indicated at 115.00-116.00 U.S. cents a kg from 115.75 cents.
June RSS1 was indicated at 165.50-166.50 Singapore cents (US$1.14-$1.15) a kg from 166.00 cents. June TSR20 was indicated at 156.75 Singapore cents (US$1.09) a kg from 157.00 cents.
